sentence: This project studies how viruses that infect humans are linked to the development of cancer, and how that could lead to therapies.
This project tries to find inherited genetic changes that affect how long men survive after a prostate cancer diagnosis.
This project builds DNA nanostructures to deliver drugs for diseases and to hold crystals used to work out molecular structures.
This project studies how dopamine signals are read by brain cells in the striatum, and how antipsychotic drugs change those signals in schizophrenia.
This project tests whether an engineered protein can help immune cells that kill tumors move into the tumor to fight cancer.
This project tests whether CRISPR can remove a repeated stretch of DNA in spinocerebellar ataxia type 12, using vesicles to deliver it into neurons.
This project builds a computational tool that measures what makes a cell a renin-expressing cell, using chromatin and gene regulation data.
This project uses chemical genetics to find out how the sodium channel in the heart works and how its faults lead to heart disease.
This project studies whether gut microbes predict which patients carry antibiotic resistant bacteria and later develop infection, using machine learning.
This project builds sequencing tools that can read chemical changes on DNA that shape gene expression, even from very small samples.
This project tests how a mobile robot can help older adults with mild memory problems, and their caregivers, in daily life.
This project studies how a mutant gene helps follicular lymphoma cells survive in their surroundings, to find ways to stop the disease from getting worse.
This project uses MRI to measure blood vessel damage, low oxygen and scarring in the hands of patients with scleroderma.
This project tries to find out how chemical changes on DNA are set up in human cells and how faulty patterns lead to disease.
This project tries to find out how limiting methionine in immune cells reduces brain damage in a mouse model of multiple sclerosis.
This project tests how gene mutations in adrenal cells lead to too much aldosterone and how the mutated genes control how much is made.
This project runs a shared imaging service that lets cancer scientists scan mice and other small animals that serve as models of cancer.
This project gets a mass spectrometer so researchers can study proteins in body fluids from people with cancer, heart disease and rare conditions.
This project studies why some patients with rheumatoid arthritis do not respond to treatment, focusing on a type of interferon.
This project studies how two proteins made by Chlamydia trachomatis change the way host cell vesicles behave and help the bacteria avoid immune defenses.
